label: DESIGN-J
per_surface_notes: ENTRY: top-nav marketing page with hero, two CTAs, a live-demo card with stats and an install command; the full page contains four very tall empty sections (only dashed corner markers) between the hero and the closing CTA — these look like canvas/WebGL effect showcases that did not render in the capture environment (other surfaces show a 'fallback rendering' toast), so they were not penalised. DISCOVERY: docs-style sidebar + 3-column card catalog (24 cards), filter tabs (Custom 24 / Shadcn 62 / React Bits 166) and an in-catalog search input, plus a global search icon. DETAIL: component page with description, tag, demo area (external demo image missing), install tabs (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun × React/Vue/Svelte/Vanilla) with copy button, Copy for AI dropdown and a floating Controls button. INTERACTION: playground with a left panel of 11 range sliders + colour swatch, Copy for AI / Share dropdowns, Reset, Back to Docs; the canvas area shows a sample landing page. No form-submit-empty capture exists and no form with a submit action is present on any surface; no click/press state was captured. The desktop DETAIL and INTERACTION 'full page' captures are identical to the first-screen captures (viewport-height only).

verdicts.reason: ENTRY uses a standard top nav (logo left, links centre, search/theme right), centred hero with one primary and one secondary CTA; DISCOVERY uses a familiar docs sidebar with grouped links, filter tabs, a search box and a 3-column card grid. The novelty (live canvas effects inside cards/demo) is the product itself and is confined to content areas.

On ENTRY the filled white pill 'Get started →' is the single primary action; 'Browse components' is a plain text/ghost button beside it (outlined on mobile). Same pattern in the closing section. On DISCOVERY/DETAIL the only filled button is 'Playground' in the sidebar, and on INTERACTION 'Back to Docs' (the filled 'Start free' buttons visible are inside the sample demo content).

ENTRY reads 1) large two-line headline, 2) grey subhead, 3) CTA pair, 4) demo card with big '24' / '100%' figures. DISCOVERY reads title 'Components' → description → filter tabs → cards; DETAIL reads 'Glass' title → description → 'Demo image' → 'Install'. Size, weight and vertical position alone number the targets.

Sidebar links sit tightly under their group labels (Getting Started / Components / Effects) with larger gaps between groups; each card keeps thumbnail, title and description together inside a bordered card; the INTERACTION panel groups the 11 sliders under a 'Controls' label separate from the Copy for AI / Share block.

The hero headline on ENTRY is surrounded by ~100px of empty space above and generous margins on both sides, far more than around the stat cards or the install row; the sample page in INTERACTION does the same around 'Ship in days, not quarters.'

The palette is near-monochrome; the high-contrast white fill acts as the action colour and appears only on primary buttons (Get started, Playground, Back to Docs) and active nav/tab pills. The only chromatic elements are the blue swatch next to 'Color #425bff' (a value readout) and a decorative nebula background at the foot of ENTRY.

Colours read as a system: near-black surfaces (#0a-ish page, slightly lighter panels and cards), three grey text tiers (white headings, light-grey body, dim labels), white as the inverted action fill, and a monospace grey for code. No stray colours appear outside the demo content and the colour-swatch readout; no semantic (error/success) colours were needed on the captured surfaces.

All inline icons are thin single-weight line icons of the same optical size: search magnifier, moon, hamburger, close ×, arrow →/←, copy squares, sliders (Controls), sparkle (Copy for AI), share nodes, reset loop and chevrons. No filled or mixed-family icons are visible.

State indicators do not rely on hue alone: the active sidebar item ('Browse All', 'Glass') and active filter tab ('Custom · 24') sit in a filled pill, active code tabs ('npm', 'React') are bolder and underlined, sliders show their numeric value as text, and the fallback state is a text notice with a close icon. No error/success indicator appears on any capture.

Volume is high (tabs show Custom 24 + Shadcn 62 + React Bits 166 items plus docs). Search is present on every surface as a header icon, DISCOVERY adds an inline 'Search custom components…' input above the grid, and the mobile ENTRY capture shows the search palette with an 'esc' key hint and keyboard-highlighted first result, indicating keyboard operation.

At 390px DISCOVERY and DETAIL hide the sidebar behind a ~44px hamburger that opens a full-screen off-canvas list with grouped links, a close button and a full-width Playground button (state-DISCOVERY-mobile-nav-open.png). ENTRY's toggle capture shows a search palette with Quick links (Introduction / Installation / Browse All) rather than the menu, still discoverable via a visible icon button; INTERACTION uses a back arrow plus a component select in the header.

Complexity is layered: catalog cards give a thumbnail + one-line summary and link to a DETAIL page; DETAIL shows one install command with package-manager/framework tabs and defers the full source ('Or copy the source below') and the tuning panel behind a 'Controls' button; INTERACTION keeps Copy for AI and Share as collapsed dropdowns.

Only hover and focus states were captured (focus ring on the logo and on the search button); no click/press state was captured for the copy buttons, Reset, sliders or Copy for AI, so immediate feedback after an action cannot be verified from the material.

The canvas/WebGL effects and playground are non-trivial to initialise, and the design shows a designed fallback toast ('You're seeing the fallback rendering…'), but no loading/skeleton state was captured on any surface, so a designed loading state cannot be confirmed.
No form is present on any surface; the only inputs are a search box and range sliders/colour picker in the playground, none of which have a submission or validation rule.

No destructive action (delete, remove, irreversible change) is visible; the only candidate is the low-stakes 'Reset' link in the playground controls, which returns ephemeral slider values to defaults.

The first 1440×900 screen states the value in one line, gives a primary 'Get started' CTA, and already shows a live demo card with '24 components', '100% open source' and a one-command install string with copy button, so core value is reached without scrolling. Mobile first screen shows headline, CTA pair and the demo card too.
The DISCOVERY catalog has a search input and filter tabs that can produce a no-results state, but no empty state was captured in any screenshot, so its content cannot be judged.

Help appears at the point of doubt: the fallback toast explains why the effect is not rendering and supplies the exact flag with a copy button; DETAIL adds the inline hint 'Move the lens over the photo to magnify every detail.' under 'Demo image'; the search palette shows an 'esc' hint; the install card is labelled 'ONE COMMAND'. No tour is used.
No multi-step flow (wizard, checkout, onboarding sequence) exists on any captured surface.
No testimonials or quotes appear on any surface; the ENTRY footer only lists library credits ('Canvas UI — David Haz', 'React Bits — David Haz').

Numbers used as proof are specific and verifiable within the product: ENTRY shows '24 Components — and counting' and '100% Open source — free forever'; DISCOVERY tabs show 'Custom · 24 / Shadcn · 62 / React Bits · 166' and the catalog indeed renders 24 cards; the footer states the licences (MIT + Commons Clause, MIT). No vague 'thousands of users' claims.

There is no pricing or signup decision point on any surface (the product is presented as free and open source; 'Get started' leads to docs). The 'Sign in / Start free' buttons visible on INTERACTION belong to the sample demo page, not the product.
No surface collects user data: there are no account, payment or contact forms, only a search box and playground sliders.
No form with submission exists on any surface, and no form-submit-empty state was captured because there was nothing to submit.
No form with required/optional fields exists; the search input is a single field and the playground sliders are tuning controls without an obligation concept.
There is no submit button or form on any surface, so submitting/success/failure states do not apply.
